AMZN.rationale: Amazon's fundamental health and trajectory are strong: accelerating revenue (+7.4% QoQ to $180.17B in Q3 2025), robust operating cash flow ($35.52B in Q3, $85B+ cumulative 3Q), a fortress balance sheet (debt-to-equity 0.149, equity +20.8% over 3Q), and Q1 2026 results showing AWS reaccelerating to 28% YoY growth with operating margin at an all-time high of 13.1%. The franchise is among the strongest in global equities with a self-reinforcing ecosystem across e-commerce (38.5-40.5% US share), AWS (~30% global cloud share, $364B backlog), advertising ($70B+ trailing, 24% growth), and Prime (215M+ members). ASCS launch into the $1.3T 3PL market and OpenAI model access on AWS are credible structural growth vectors. However, valuation is the binding constraint: P/E of 37.89x sits at the very top of its 365-day range (28.2-39.0x), having expanded +25.7% from the March trough without a corresponding margin inflection (net margin flat at 11.1%). The stock surged +33.9% in one quarter against only +7.4% QoQ revenue growth — a ~5x leverage of price to fundamentals. Q3 2025 operating margin actually compressed to 9.7% from 11.4% in Q2. Rising 10Y yields (4.47%) and oil ($104.66/bbl) are macro headwinds for a 38x P/E stock with logistics cost exposure. The $200B 2026 capex commitment compresses trailing FCF to ~$11.2B. Near-term catalysts exist (Q1 2026 beat, ASCS launch, OpenAI partnership shift) but are largely priced in after the +34% run. Net: excellent business, but the stock is priced near-perfection at the top of its valuation range, leaving limited upside from current levels.
